primary_diagnosis_treated: Uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy (CKD stage 4)
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease) and NICE NG28 (Type 2 diabetes)

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after any dose change
medications.purpose: Renal protection, proteinuria reduction and hypertension control in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; up‑titrate to maximally tolerated dose.

medications.purpose: High‑intensity lipid‑lowering for cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises a statin for all CKD patients; atorvastatin 20 mg is the recommended high‑intensity option.

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and monitor renal function
medications.purpose: Slows CKD progression and improves glycaemic control in diabetes with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NG203 and NG28 list dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for CKD with ACR ≥ 22.6 mg/mmol or eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m².

medications.dose: 0.25 mg weekly, titrate to 0.5 mg after 4 weeks and up to 1 mg as needed
medications.purpose: Additional glucose lowering, weight loss and cardiovascular risk reduction
medications.nice_justification: NG28 recommends GLP‑1 RA (e.g., semaglutide) for T2DM with obesity or established CVD.

medications.dose: 200 mg three times daily with vitamin C
medications.duration: Until ferritin >100 µg/L and TSAT >20 % – reassess after 3 months
medications.purpose: Correct iron‑deficiency anaemia before considering ESA therapy
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends treating iron deficiency before ESA in CKD‑related anaemia.

medications.duration: Lifelong – review blood pressure in 2 weeks and titrate if needed
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive if target BP (<140/90 mmHg) not achieved with ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises additional agents (e.g., CCB) to reach BP targets in CKD.

medications.duration: To be discontinued and replaced by atorvastatin
medications.nice_justification: Existing medication; replaced per NG203 recommendation for high‑intensity statin.

medications.dose: 25 mg as needed for pruritus or sleep
Apply to affected skin twice daily

interactions_checked.interaction: Both can affect renal function and potassium; risk of acute kidney injury or hyperkalaemia.
interactions_checked.action: Check serum creatinine and potassium 1‑2 weeks after dose change; ensure adequate hydration.

interactions_checked.interaction: Concurrent use increases risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
Iron may cause gastrointestinal irritation; advise taking iron at least 2 hours apart from semaglutide.

contraindications.reason: eGFR is likely <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD stage 4) – risk of lactic acidosis.
contraindications.alternative: DPP‑4 inhibitor (e.g., linagliptin 5 mg daily) if SGLT2‑i unsuitable.

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 4 – NSAIDs accelerate renal decline and cause fluid retention.
Guideline contraindicates dual RAAS blockade due to hyperkalaemia and AKI risk.
Risk of fluid retention and heart failure; patient has CKD and potential HF risk.
Prolonged hypoglycaemia risk in severe renal impairment.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m² to allow dapagliflozin; if eGFR <20, switch to DPP‑4 inhibitor.
Serum potassium not available – assumed ≤5.0 mmol/L; will monitor after ACE‑I up‑titration.
Albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio not provided – assumed ≥22.6 mg/mmol to meet SGLT2‑i indication.
HbA1c not provided – assumed >48 mmol/mol; will confirm before titrating semaglutide.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not available – oral iron prescribed pending results; ESA only after iron repletion.
Allergy status unknown – will verify before starting new agents (especially statin and GLP‑1 RA).
Liver function tests not provided – required before initiating atorvastatin 20 mg.
Blood pressure values not provided – amlodipine added only if target BP not achieved with ACE‑I alone.
treatment_summary: The plan up‑titrates lisinopril to 20 mg, switches to high‑intensity atorvastatin 20 mg, adds dapagliflozin 10 mg daily and semaglutide weekly to control diabetes and protect kidney function, introduces oral iron pending iron studies, and adds amlodipine 5 mg if hypertension remains uncontrolled. Existing medications are reviewed for safety, and all drug interactions and contraindications have been checked against NICE NG203 and NG28. Monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, lipid profile, HbA1c, and anemia parameters is outlined, with regular review intervals.
